title: Economic Analyst Position
industry: Economics, Economics and Social Sciences, General Economics (JEL A), Finance
text:
Description:
Role Purpose:
Support economic and financial analysis of utility networks by evaluating CAPEX, OPEX, lifecycle costs, and investment decisions to improve cost efficiency, resilience, and service performance.
Key Responsibilities:
Data Assessment: Identify data gaps, assess data quality, and recommend improvements for cost analysis.
Benchmarking: Analyze CAPEX, OPEX, and maintenance costs; benchmark against international utilities; identify efficiency gaps.
Techno-Economic Analysis: Evaluate Security of Supply Standards (SoSS), resilience, and service levels; assess cost vs reliability trade-offs.
Value Engineering: Conduct lifecycle cost analysis; identify cost-saving design and material alternatives.
Standards & Specifications: Perform cost-benefit analyses for new technologies and standards; support investment decisions.
Digital Tools Support: Develop cost models and support investment prioritization tools.
Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field.
Professional certifications preferred (e.g., CFA, CPA, or FMVA).
Advanced degree (MBA / MSc Finance) desirable.
Minimum 10 years of work experience.
Experience in water, energy or infrastructure sectors preferred.
Preferred Specifications:
CAPEX/OPEX budgeting, forecasting, and variance analysis.
Financial modelling and business case evaluation (ROI, NPV).
Strong accounting knowledge (cost allocation, capitalization).
Advanced Excel and ERP systems (e.g., SAP) proficiency.
Data analysis and reporting (insight generation for decision-making).
Stakeholder coordination with finance, engineering, and operations teams.
Cost-benefit and investment analysis (NPV, IRR).
